Lessons.Title: Solve Problems Using the Four Operations
ExplanationParagraphs: Original warm-up: A farmer picked apples; some apples are packed equally into boxes and some are loose. The story initially has no numbers. Pupils suggest questions and quantities rather than being given a fabricated fixed answer.

Activity1 Apple Adventure source figure is a precise list of TWELVE numbers:400,300,240,12,350,290,230,10,340,280,170,5. Choose four such that TOTAL=LOOSE + NUMBER_OF_BOXES × APPLES_PER_BOX. Source does not mandate a unique selection. E.g.400=280+10×12,350=290+5×12,340=280+5×12,300=240+5×12,230=170+5×12. Teacher judges chosen tuples and unit labels.

Public teacher synthesis separately displays a sample that uses200 total,152 apples loose and8 boxes, therefore(200−152)÷8=6 apples per box. Those numbers are NOT in the original activity's twelve-number choice list; do not mistake them for given selections.
Activity2 Apple Days Tyler's display:85 apples total,5 rows of10 in display, so85−(5×10)=35 apples left. Equation5×10+n=85, n=35.
Clare's cash box: after eight brownies at$3 each the box has$125. Earlier cash c satisfies c+8×3=125, c=101 dollars.
Applesauce jars:200 originally,184 sold, remaining16 divided among4 workers gives(200−184)÷4=4 jars per worker.
Student section summary original52÷4=13, shown as four groups of one ten and three ones, or4×(10+3)=52. Interpret unknowns through base-ten diagrams.

Four original visual assets inspected: number-list SVG, orchard-barn illustration, apple-tree photograph and four groups of13 base-ten SVG. App uses new first-party math models, not copied source pixels. Gated Apples at the Farm Stand Cool-down and Stage D/tests remain outside closure.

KeyConcepts.Title: Two-step word problems
KeyConcepts.Definition: Apply operations in a meaningful order to find an unknown.

KeyConcepts.Title: Boxes and loose apples
KeyConcepts.Definition: Total equals packed boxes plus loose apples.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unknown letter
KeyConcepts.Definition: Letter represents the missing amount in a contextual equation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Inverse operations
KeyConcepts.Definition: Subtract before dividing when removing sold items or unpacked items.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat Apple's number-list problem as having one exact numeric solution.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Pupils are asked to choose four source numbers that satisfy a relationship; many work.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Validate total=loose+boxes×perBox, not one prescribed tuple.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Use teacher example200,152,8 as original activity choices.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: These sample numbers are displayed only later for discussion, not on the original source list.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep source list and teacher illustration separate.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Say the applesauce jars result is16 per person.
